assessments.reasoning: The six verified publisher slices define coverage and the two forms, give the section 3.1 source terms, and connect the executable-distribution trigger to every access condition in paragraph (a).

challenge.method: Tested three offers independently: accessible source with no directions to recipients, prompt access at a charge above distribution cost, and cost-price access after an unreasonable delay.
challenge.results: Each offer fails a different condition. A high absolute price requires a cost comparison, and elapsed time requires a timeliness assessment. The clause specifies neither a fixed price nor a universal deadline.

limitations: The obligation concerns the Covered Software. Reasonableness, timeliness and distribution cost depend on facts. Section 4 governs legal impossibility.
reasoning: Section 3.2(a) requires both availability of the covered source under section 3.1 and information that tells executable recipients how to obtain it. The means must be reasonable, delivery timely, and the charge at most the cost of distribution to that recipient.
